description: Per time in force, count every matched risk/margin record and take its share of the overall record total.

a.request: For each time-in-force value (`orders.timespan`), looking at risk/margin records matched to their order (`riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault`; unmatched records dropped), show the time in force, the number of risk/margin records (an order with several records counts once per record), that number's share of the total across all time-in-force values, and how much the share differs from the average share across the time-in-force values. Don't round.
a.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT o.timespan, COUNT(*) AS risk_margin_records FROM orders AS o JOIN riskandmargin AS r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), shares AS (SELECT timespan, risk_margin_records, risk_margin_records::numeric / SUM(risk_margin_records) OVER () AS share FROM counts) SELECT timespan, risk_margin_records, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS difference_from_average_share FROM shares ORDER BY timespan;

c.request: For each time in force, using risk/margin records matched to their orders (`riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault`; unmatched dropped), show the time in force, its risk/margin count, that count's share of the overall total, and how far the share is from the average share across time-in-force values. No rounding. Per time in force, count every matched risk/margin record and take its share of the overall record total.
c.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT o.timespan AS time_in_force, COUNT(*) AS risk_margin_count FROM riskandmargin AS r JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), shares AS (SELECT time_in_force, risk_margin_count, risk_margin_count::numeric / SUM(risk_margin_count) OVER () AS share FROM counts) SELECT time_in_force, risk_margin_count, share, ABS(share - AVG(share) OVER ()) AS distance_from_average_share FROM shares ORDER BY time_in_force;

b.request: For each time-in-force value, count all risk/margin records whose `ordervault` matches an order’s `recordvault`, divide that count by the total count of all matched risk/margin records, and show the time in force, count, unrounded share, and unrounded difference between that share and the average share across time-in-force values
b.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT o.timespan AS time_in_force, COUNT(*) AS risk_margin_count FROM riskandmargin AS rm JOIN orders AS o ON rm.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), shares AS (SELECT time_in_force, risk_margin_count, risk_margin_count::numeric / SUM(risk_margin_count) OVER () AS share FROM counts) SELECT time_in_force, risk_margin_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS difference_from_average_share FROM shares ORDER BY time_in_force;

d.request: For each time-in-force value, how many risk/margin records match an order (`riskandmargin.ordervault = orders.recordvault`), and what share of the total matched risk/margin records does that count represent? Exclude unmatched records and do not round.
d.sql: SELECT o.timespan, COUNT(*) AS risk_margin_count, COUNT(*)::numeric / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share_of_total FROM riskandmargin AS r JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan ORDER BY o.timespan;
